newsitem.title: USA: BFS CEO says suitor initiated contact.
newsitem.headline: BFS CEO says suitor initiated contact.

text.p: BFS Bankorp Inc, a thrift with $621 million in assets, hired investment bank Keefe, Bruyette & Woods after it was approached by a suitor, president and chief executive James Randall said Friday in a telephone interview.
In a news release Thursday, BFS Bankorp said Keefe, Bruyette would explore strategic alternatives to enhancing shareholder value.
The news release did not identify any of the parties with which which BFS has had preliminary discussions and Randall declined to mention any names.
"We were not looking to sell, we were approached by somebody which is what started this," Randall said. "Since then we had additional discussions with a couple of parties as well."

Asked how long it might take for a deal to be put together, Randall responded, "something could happen quickly or it could take longer or it may never happen if they are not willing to pay a reasonable price."
BFS Bankorp is the holding company for Bankers Federal Savings FSB which has five branches in New York City. Bankers Federal specializes in lending to the multi-family residential markett.
About 55 percent of the 1.6 milliion outstanding shares are owned by Fredric Gould, an outside director.
A decision to sell the company rests with the board of directors.
BFS Bankorp was up 1-1/2 to 51 in early afternoon.
